mainTopic: The special status of סוריא, and a slave's freedom document that also gives property
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the special in-between status of סוריא and explains each of its laws. The תנא who obligates סוריא in מעשר and שביעית holds that כיבוש יחיד counts as a real conquest. A person can enter סוריא in טהרה by being carried inside a closed box. That works because the חכמים decreed טומאה only on סוריא's soil, not on its air. רב ששת explains that comparing a field in סוריא to one near ירושלים means a bill of sale may be written for it even on שבת. The writing is done by a גוי, and the חכמים lifted their usual ban for the sake of ישוב ארץ ישראל. The גמרא then turns to a slave who brings his own freedom document that also gives him his master's property. אביי tries two opposite rulings, and רבא rejects both. רבא rules that the slave goes free but does not get the property. רב אדא בר מתנה says this follows only רבי שמעון, who holds that a statement can be divided, and the גמרא begins quoting the משנה in פאה. That quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: buying a field in Syria
steps.stepSummary: The last clause of the ברייתא: buying a field in סוריא is like buying one near ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who buys a field in Syria] is like one who buys it in the outskirts of Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the final words of a ברייתא, started earlier, that lists special laws about סוריא. The גמרא will now go back and explain its parts one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats סוריא as being in between: in some ways it is like חוץ לארץ, and in other ways it is like ארץ ישראל. This last clause compares a purchase there to a purchase right next to ירושלים. Steps 7 and 8 explain what that comparison means in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, the lands that דוד המלך conquered outside the main borders of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: is like one who buys it in the outskirts of Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that began on the previous daf: 'one who buys a field in Syria…'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying a field in סוריא is treated like buying a field in the outskirts of ירושלים.

steps.title: Why Syria is obligated in tithes and the Sabbatical year
steps.stepSummary: The תנא who obligates סוריא in מעשר and שביעית holds that כיבוש יחיד counts as a real conquest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling that Syria is obligated in tithes and the Sabbatical year like the Land of Israel: this תנא holds that a conquest by an individual is called a conquest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the ברייתא's ruling that סוריא must keep מעשר and שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוריא was conquered by דוד on his own initiative, not as part of the whole nation's conquest. Whether such a 'private' conquest gives the land the holiness of ארץ ישראל depends on whether כיבוש יחיד counts. This תנא says it does, so the land-based מצוות apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: a conquest by an individual, not by the whole nation

phrases.english: It is obligated in tithes and the Sabbatical year like the Land of Israel –
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא's earlier line about Syria.

phrases.english: he holds that a conquest by an individual is called a conquest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explain one clause of the ברייתא just completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view that obligates סוריא in מעשר and שביעית is based on כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that סוריא's halachic status depends on a basic מחלוקת about what kind of conquest makes land holy.

steps.title: How can one enter Syria in purity if its soil is impure?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says one may enter סוריא in טהרה, but it also said its soil is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who wants to enter it in purity may enter.' But didn't you say its soil is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and points out that it seems to contradict the ברייתא's own first rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא started by saying the soil of סוריא makes a person טמא, like חוץ לארץ. If so, walking into סוריא should make anyone טמא right away. So how can the ברייתא say a person can enter it and stay טהור?

keyTerms.meaning: in a state of ritual purity

phrases.english: And one who wants to enter it in purity may enter –
But didn't you say its soil is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's clause that one may enter סוריא in טהרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: if the soil is טמא, entering should automatically make a person טמא.

steps.title: He enters inside a chest, box, or cabinet
steps.stepSummary: The person enters סוריא sealed inside a closed container, so he never touches the soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a chest, a box, or a cabinet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא means a person who is carried in inside a closed container.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of סוריא is in its soil. A person riding inside a closed container never touches that soil, so he stays טהור. Both rules of the ברייתא can therefore be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: a large chest or closed carriage
a cabinet, a tall closed cupboard

phrases.english: In a chest, a box, or a cabinet.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific way of entering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Entering סוריא means walking on its soil, so a person must become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about someone carried in inside a closed container, who never touches the soil.

steps.title: A ברייתא: entering foreign lands in a closed container
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת: רבי says entering חוץ לארץ in a closed container makes one טמא, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One who enters the land of the nations in a chest, a box, or a cabinet – רבי declares him impure, and רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה declares him pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source showing that being inside a container can matter for טומאה. This sets up the next line, which explains how it applies to סוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About other foreign lands there is a מחלוקת. רבי is strict even when a person is inside a container, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is lenient. At first glance רבי's view seems to go against the answer just given about סוריא, and the next step deals with that.

keyTerms.meaning: the land of the nations, meaning any land outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who enters the land of the nations
in a chest, a box, or a cabinet – Rabbi declares him impure,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here, with no other name, means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda declares him pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the answer of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that entering in a closed container keeps a person טהור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a מחלוקת between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about entering foreign lands in a container.

steps.title: Even רבי agrees that Syria's air is not impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי is strict only in other foreign lands, where both the soil and the air were made טמא. In סוריא only the soil was made טמא, so everyone agrees a container protects.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי declares him impure only in the land of the nations, where they decreed on its clumps of soil and on its air. But Syria – they decreed on its clumps of soil; they did not decree on its air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי's strict view does not apply to סוריא. So the answer about entering in a container works according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other foreign lands carry a decree of טומאה on both their soil and their air, so even being inside a container does not help according to רבי. In סוריא the decree covers only the soil. A closed container keeps the person off the soil, so he stays טהור according to all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: its clumps of earth, its soil
its air, the space above the land

steps.whatToRemember: סוריא's טומאה is only in its soil, not its air. So a person carried in inside a closed container stays טהור according to everyone, even רבי.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi declares impure
only in the land of the nations,
where they decreed on its clumps of soil and on its air,
but Syria – they decreed on its clumps of soil,
they did not decree on its air.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי לָא קָא מְטַמֵּא אֶלָּא בְּאֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by showing that even רבי's strict view does not apply to סוריא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer of step 4, now shown to hold according to all opinions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The distinction between a decree on both soil and air (other foreign lands) and a decree on soil alone (סוריא).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that סוריא's טומאה is milder than that of other foreign lands, which fits its in-between status.

steps.title: What is the practical point of comparing Syria to Jerusalem's outskirts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law comes from saying a field bought in סוריא is like one bought near ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who buys a field in Syria is like one who buys it in the outskirts of Jerusalem.' For what law is this stated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last clause of the ברייתא and asks what practical difference it makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison sounds like a general statement of importance, but the גמרא wants to know the concrete הלכה behind it. The question is not an attack. It asks for the practical meaning of the line.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? what is the practical point?

phrases.english: And one who buys a field in Syria
is like one who buys it in the outskirts of Jerusalem –
for what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's final clause (from step 1) to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halachic consequence of comparing a field in סוריא to a field near ירושלים.

steps.title: רב ששת: a bill of sale may be written, even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the comparison teaches that a bill of sale may be written for a field in סוריא, even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: To say that one writes a bill of sale for it, and even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question: buying land in סוריא is so important that a bill of sale may be written for it even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying land near ירושלים is treated as settling ארץ ישראל, which is a very important מצוה. By putting סוריא in the same category, the ברייתא allows a bill of sale for such a purchase even on שבת. Step 10 explains how writing on שבת can be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a bill of sale, a document recording a purchase

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת means a Jew may write with his own hand on שבת. The גמרא is about to explain how this works in a permitted way.
steps.whatToRemember: Buying land in סוריא is treated like settling ארץ ישראל, so a bill of sale may be written for it even on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
To say that one writes a bill of sale for it,
and even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לוֹמַר שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו אוֹנוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison teaches that a bill of sale may be written for a field bought in סוריא, even on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next discussion about how writing on שבת can be allowed for the sake of settling the land.

steps.title: How Can One Write on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: writing on שבת is a full Torah prohibition, so how can a sale document be written then?
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת? Can you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is shocked by רב ששת's answer that a sale document for a field in סוריא may be written even on שבת. Writing is one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing on שבת is a Torah-level מלאכה, so no reason, even settling the land, could simply allow a Jew to do it himself. This is a challenge against the plain meaning of רב ששת's words. The next step will explain what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (an expression of surprise)
The Sabbath, when writing is a forbidden מלאכה

phrases.english: On Shabbat? Can it enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'even on שבת' part of רב ששת's answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's statement that a sale document for a field in סוריא may be written on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Writing is a Torah-level מלאכה on שבת, so it cannot be allowed just to buy land.

steps.title: Telling a Non-Jew to Write It
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a Jew tells a גוי to write the document. Normally that is a rabbinic prohibition (שבות), but the חכמים did not forbid it here because of ישוב ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: one tells a גוי and the גוי does it. Here too, one tells a גוי and he writes it. And even though telling a גוי to do a forbidden act is a rabbinic prohibition, the חכמים did not make that rule here, because of settling ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the Jew does not write on שבת himself. He asks a גוי to write it, and the חכמים allowed this for the sake of settling the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah prohibition is avoided, because the גוי does the writing. Asking a גוי is normally forbidden by the חכמים (אמירה לגוי is a שבות), but because ישוב ארץ ישראל is so important, they did not apply their rule in this case. Since סוריא was compared to near ירושלים, the same leniency applies there.

keyTerms.meaning: Telling a non-Jew to do a forbidden act for a Jew on שבת
The מצוה of settling the Land of Israel
The חכמים did not make a decree here

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how far the חכמים went for ישוב ארץ ישראל: they set aside their own שבת rule for it.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
one tells a gentile and he does it;
here too, one tells a gentile and he does it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמִירָה לְגוֹי שְׁבוּת,
phrases.english: And even though telling a gentile is a rabbinic prohibition,
because of settling Eretz Yisrael –
the Sages did not decree it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9 by explaining how the writing is done.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case: the writing is done by a גוי, not by the Jew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת seemed to allow a Jew to write on שבת himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי writes it at a Jew's request. The usual rabbinic ban on this is lifted for ישוב ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: Buying land in ארץ ישראל (and סוריא) is so important that a Jew may ask a גוי to write the sale document even on שבת.

steps.title: A Slave Brings His Freedom Document
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: a ברייתא teaches that if a slave brings his freedom document saying 'yourself and my property are yours,' he becomes free but does not get the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: a slave brought his freedom document, and it says 'You yourself and my property are given to you.' He acquires himself, but he does not acquire the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new subject with a ברייתא about a slave who brings his own freedom document to court. The document gives him both his freedom and his master's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling splits the document in two. Freeing himself works right away, but taking the property does not, because the property part is a normal money document that needs the usual confirmation. Notice that the document lists 'yourself' and 'my property' as two separate things.

keyTerms.meaning: His document, here the slave's freedom document (גט שחרור)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A slave who brought his document of release,
and it is written in it:
"You yourself and my property are acquired by you,"
himself – he acquired,
phrases.notes: This means he is now a free man.

phrases.english: the property – he did not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, separate from the סוריא discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave bringing his own document saying 'yourself and my property' gains his freedom but not the property.

steps.title: What If It Says 'All My Property'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a document that says 'all my property is yours' without mentioning the slave separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if it says 'All my property is given to you,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new case. The document does not name the slave himself. It only says 'all my property.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave counts as his master's property, so 'all my property' includes the slave too. The question is whether the freedom and the property now come from one single phrase, and whether that changes the ברייתא's split ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
"All my property is acquired by you" – what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא of Step 11 with a slightly different wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a slave acquires the property when the document says 'all my property,' a phrase that also includes himself

steps.title: אביי: Freedom Brings the Property Along
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that because the slave acquires himself through this document, he also acquires the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: since he acquired himself, he also acquired the property.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He says the slave gets the property too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'all my property' is one phrase that covers both the slave and the other property. The phrase clearly works for the slave's freedom, so אביי holds it must work for the rest of the property as well. This is different from the ברייתא, where the two were written separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because (one thing works, so the other does too)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
since he acquired himself,
phrases.notes: He is part of 'all my property,' and that phrase made him free.

phrases.english: he acquired the property.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The slave acquires the property too, since the same phrase that frees him also covers the property.

steps.title: רבא: Property Still Needs Confirmation
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: freedom should work like a woman's גט, but property should follow the normal rule that documents need court confirmation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It makes sense that he acquires himself, just like a woman's גט. But he should not acquire the property, just like the confirmation of all ordinary documents!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against אביי. He says the slave's freedom and the property follow two different rules, even if one phrase covers both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freedom is like a woman's גט: someone who brings it can rely on it. The property part is a regular money document, and regular documents need קיום שטרות (confirmation by their witnesses) before a court relies on them. So רבא holds the property should not be acquired without that confirmation, which is the same split the ברייתא made.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the slave stays a slave. He agrees the slave goes free. He only argues about the property.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
It makes sense that he acquires himself,
just as with a woman's bill of divorce,
but the property he should not acquire,
just as with the confirmation of ordinary documents!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: בִּשְׁלָמָא עַצְמוֹ לִיקְנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that the slave acquires the property along with himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two parts follow different rules. Freedom is like a woman's גט, which works when brought. Property is like any money document, which needs קיום שטרות. One phrase covering both should not change that.

steps.title: אביי reverses himself: no property means no freedom
steps.stepSummary: After רבא's challenge, אביי flips his position. Since the slave does not get the property, he does not get his freedom either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי then said: Since he did not acquire the property, he did not acquire himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי responds to רבא's challenge by switching his ruling. Now the slave gets neither himself nor the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, אביי tied the two together in one direction: getting himself meant getting the property too. Now he keeps them tied together but reverses the direction. The property cannot be acquired without court confirmation, so the freedom fails as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back / then (he changed his mind)
Since / because of (one thing leads to the other)

phrases.english: Abaye then said:
phrases.notes: "הדר" tells you אביי is going back on what he said in Step 13.

phrases.english: Since he did not acquire the property,
he did not acquire himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers רבא's challenge from Step 14 by reversing his ruling from Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the slave acquires himself, he also acquires the property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the slave does not acquire the property, he does not acquire himself either.

steps.title: רבא: freedom should still work like a woman's divorce document
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees the property should not be acquired. But he argues the freedom should still work, just as a woman can bring her own גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Granted, he should not acquire the property, just as with confirming ordinary documents. But he should acquire himself, just as with a woman's divorce document!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's new position. He agrees about the property, but he holds the freedom should still take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sees two separate rules for two separate parts of the document. Property needs court confirmation, like any document. Freedom follows the rule of a woman's גט, which she may bring herself. So one part failing should not knock out the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as it is with... (comparison to a known case)
Court confirmation of a document's signatures

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Granted, the property he should not acquire,
just as with the confirmation of ordinary documents;
but himself he should acquire,
just as with a woman's divorce document!
phrases.notes: A woman can bring her own גט and be believed about it, as רבא said in Step 14.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: בִּשְׁלָמָא נְכָסִים לָא לִיקְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's reversed ruling in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that failing to get the property means failing to get freedom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Freedom and property follow different rules (גט אשה versus קיום שטרות), so they should not stand or fall together.

steps.title: רבא's ruling: freedom yes, property no, in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own ruling. Whether the document says 'yourself and my property' or 'all my property,' the slave goes free but does not get the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: In both this case and that case, he acquires himself but does not acquire the property.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected both of אביי's positions, רבא states his own rule. It covers both kinds of document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא applies the earlier ברייתא's ruling (Step 11) to the 'all my property' case as well. He splits the document's effect: the freedom part works, and the property part waits for court confirmation.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (both cases alike)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: a slave who brings his own freedom document goes free, but he does not get the property written in it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
both this and that,
phrases.notes: He means both kinds of document: "yourself and my property" and "all my property."

phrases.english: himself, he acquires;
the property, he does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's two rejected positions with רבא's own ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both cases the slave acquires his freedom but not the property.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנה: your view follows only רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה asks which תנא רבא follows. His answer: only רבי שמעון, who holds that one statement can be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to רבא: In accordance with whom? In accordance with רבי שמעון, who says we divide a statement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה challenges רבא. He argues that רבא's ruling depends on one specific opinion, that of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא accepts half of one document (the freedom) and rejects the other half (the property). That is exactly 'dividing a statement.' The challenge implies that רבא's ruling would not hold for anyone who disagrees with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: We divide a statement (accept part, reject part)

steps.confusionAlert: Splitting here is not about cutting the paper. It means one document can be accepted for one thing (freedom) and rejected for another (property).

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Rava:
In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
who says we divide a statement;
phrases.notes: One statement can be accepted in part and rejected in part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרָבָא: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from Step 17 by tying it to one specific opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the slave gets his freedom but not the property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accepting half a document requires the view that a statement can be divided, which is the view of רבי שמעון alone.

steps.title: The source: a master who writes all his property to his slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה as the source for the debate about dividing a statement. The first view holds that if the master kept any land, the slave is not freed. רבי שמעון's view begins here.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who writes all his property to his slave, the slave goes free. If he kept for himself any amount of land, the slave does not go free. רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows where רבי שמעון's idea of dividing a statement comes from. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says that if the master kept back any land for himself, the slave does not go free, since perhaps the master kept the slave back as well. רבי שמעון disagrees, and his words begin right here.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out a free man (was freed)
Any amount of land, even a tiny bit

phrases.english: As we learned: One who writes all his property to his slave,
he goes out a free man.
If he kept back any amount of land,
he does not go out a free man.

steps.raayaObject: That dividing a statement is the view of רבי שמעון, in a dispute with the first opinion
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פאה ג:ח about a master writing all his property to his slave
